newsitem.title: USA: Dlr ends up in US on rate hopes and Hesse comments.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends up in US on rate hopes and Hesse comments.

text.p: The dollar closed firmer amid growing hopes for higher U.S. interest rates and a news report that a senior German central bank official did not object to recent dollar gains versus the mark, experts said.
Yet a sharp sell-off in the prices of Treasury securities and stocks caused the dollar to trim its gains.
The Commerce Department reported that sales by retail stores rose 0.8 percent in February after gaining a revised 1.5 percent in January, the strongest rise in nearly a year.
The sales data indicated the economy is growing at a robust pace in the first quarter of this year.
Some traders wondered whether the Federal Reserve will need to hike short-term interest rates to keep the economy from overheating.
Fed policymakers meet on March 25.

"I think the feeling was that there's more chance for a rate rise in March unsettled the market a little bit. And we saw bonds come off and a rise in the value of the dollar," said Stephen Jury, chief dealer at Union Bank of Switzerland.
The dollar rose above 123 Japanese yen for the first time in nearly three weeks. As the dollar rallied, it triggered previously set orders to buy, hastening the currency's rise.
The dollar closed at 123.40/45 yen, up from 122.65/70 yen at the open. Against the mark, the dollar finished at 1.7050/60 marks from 1.6951/54 marks.
The dollar got another shot in the arm after a news report that Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said there was no reason for the Bundesbank to take action on the stronger dollar.
Hesse also reportedly said the stronger dollar recently is not an indication of a new trend.
Since the beginning of the year, the dollar has risen nearly 12 percent versus the mark.
"We were right below some triggers, and as soon as he spoke in thin markets, people bought (dollars)... So, off we went," said Kevin Harris, an international economist at MCM CurrencyWatch.
He attributed dollar gains partly to a "short squeeze".
Late in the day, the dollar rally paused when the price of the 30-year bond fell one point and the Dow Jones industrial average tumbled more than 2.0 percent.
The Dow fell 160 points to close unofficially at 6879, representing the fifth steepest fall in point terms in the history of the average.

"Obviously the sell-off in the stocks and bonds are weighing on the dollar, but there has been some very good interest to buy dollars today," said John McCarthy, senior vice president of foreign exchange at ING Capital Markets.
"For the dollar to put in a strong performance like today in the face of a weaker stock and bond market is pretty impressive," he added.
Elsewhere, the dollar closed at 1.4650/60 Swiss francs, up from 1.4524/31 francs at the open.
Sterling slid to $1.5955/65 from $1.6015/25. The dollar climbed to Canadian $1.3653/58 from C$1.3615/20.
The Australian dollar ended at $0.7927/32, up slightly from $0.7921/26.
